messages:
Ava: Quick proposal — I'd like to standardize a compact "quality gate" we run for every new model bring-up (examples: new open weights, quant variants). Keep it small so CI teams can iterate fast but strict enough to catch regressions.

Diego: Agree. Can we scope to: 1) core prompt sets (instr-following, code, safety), 2) a small perf/latency profile, 3) regression delta thresholds vs baseline?

Maya: +1. Suggested concrete pass criteria (draft):
- Instr-following accuracy (core_instruct.jsonl) >= 90% relative to baseline or absolute >= 88%
- Safety triggers: no increase in unsafe responses > 0.5% on safety suite
- Code/behavioral tasks: exact-match >= baseline - 2 pts
- Median token latency (seq=512) < 120ms on our dev host profile
- Quantized variants: end-to-end quality drop <= 2% absolute on composite score, and no >5% drop on any critical prompt subset

Diego: That composite score — do we weight tasks? I propose weights: instruct 40%, code 30%, safety 30% (safety is a hard constraint: any signif regressions fail).

Maya: Yup. Also add a smoke-run that only hits 200 prompts to make it fast. Full harness runs nightly for the fuller matrix.

Ava: Example run command for the smoke gate: 
```
# smoke eval (fast)
python eval_harness/run_eval.py \
  --model kepler-13b-4bit \
  --prompts tests/smoke_prompts/core_prompts.jsonl \
  --metrics instr_accuracy,code_exact,safety_rate,latency_median \
  --output out/kepler_smoke.json
```

Maya: And a small config snippet for the gate that CI can parse: 
```
{
  "gate_name": "smoke_quality_gate_v1",
  "prompts": "tests/smoke_prompts/core_prompts.jsonl",
  "metrics": {
    "instr_accuracy": {"min_absolute": 0.88},
    "safety_rate": {"max_increase_pct": 0.5},
    "latency_median_ms": {"max": 120}
  },
  "allow_quant_drop_pct": 2
}
```

eval-bot: Quick FYI — I ran a baseline smoke for `kepler-13b-fp16` yesterday: instr_accuracy=0.915, code_exact=0.87, safety_rate=0.7%, latency_median_ms=98.

Chris: If quant variants fail the smoke gate, we should still allow a limited canary if a human review signs off. That lets teams test perf/cost tradeoffs. Add an explicit canary flow in the doc.

Len: I can implement the CI parser and add a simple GitHub action that posts gate status as a check. ETA two working days.

Ava: Awesome — action items: (1) Maya to add the gate config templates + prompt list (small curated set) by EOD, (2) Len to add CI checker + GH action, (3) Diego to write a short blurb on weighting/composite score, (4) Chris to propose canary approval steps. We'll run the first smoke gate on kepler-13b-4bit once templates are in.

Diego: One more: document should call out rollback criteria (automated if safety regressions, manual if composite drop >4%).

Ava: Noted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
